subject: Recap: SaaS.ai discovery — API transition & open-model pilot next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@saas.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: SaaS.ai discovery — API transition & open-model pilot next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap so we have a shared starting point and clear next steps. Let me know if I missed or misstated anything.

What we heard (top pain points)
- Token and inference spend is a major drag: ~$120k/month on LLM API (OpenAI + Anthropic) and growing with product usage.
- Vendor lock-in and rate limits are causing operational headaches during spikes.
- Need parity on function-calling/streaming and embeddings (current vector search workflows are critical).
- Safety / hallucination controls for billing/customer-facing summaries are a high bar — you need measurable equivalence on top intents.

Current stack (as shared)
- Front-end chat UI (React) -> Node.js API layer -> microservices (K8s) calling OpenAI (chat + embeddings) and Anthropic for specific intents.
- Vector DB: Pinecone for embeddings + approximate nearest neighbor.
- Messaging backbone: Kafka for ingestion and async job processing.
- Monthly volume: ~2M LLM calls/month, peak concurrency ~200–300 qps, typical prompt length 150–600 tokens, embedding dims 1536.

Success criteria for pilot / evaluation
- Quality: parity on top-3 intents (FAQ answer accuracy, transaction extraction, and billing-summary generation) vs current production models.
- Latency: maintain end-to-end 95th percentile <= 400ms for interactive chat flows.
- Cost: demonstrable unit-cost reduction (targeting >= 2.5x improvement) at pilot scale.
- Integration: OpenAI-compatible surface (chat/completions/embeddings), streaming & function-calling support, and minimal client SDK changes.
- Security: SOC 2 evidence + VPC-friendly deployment options for later stages.

Model shortlist we discussed (initial candidates)
- Llama-2-chat-70B (quantized variants for cost)
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (good for instruction tuning workloads)
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (lighter-weight option for embeddings/fast inference)

Compatibility notes
- Need support for OpenAI-like embeddings shape and semantics (1536 dims), or a migration path with tooling to re-index.
- Streaming + function-calling parity is mandatory for chat UX.
- Prefix/KV cache behavior and determinism for billing-summary prompts needs validation.

Proposed next steps
1) You send 3–5 representative prompt sets + a redacted traffic snapshot (we requested the CSV during the call).
2) Redwood runs an initial cost/latency estimate and proposes a minimal pilot config (we typically suggest a 2-GPU Dedicated pilot for throughput parity).
3) Technical deep dive with your infra lead and our SE (Aditya) — target week of Jun 15.
4) Draft SOW and POC terms (we'll attach a first-pass SOW).

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (first-pass), guidance checklist.

If that aligns, I'll schedule the technical deep-dive and send over a DocuSign-friendly SOW for review.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Thanks Elena — a couple of technical clarifying Qs to prep for the deep-dive:
1) Embedding details: you noted 1536 dims today — is that fixed for all datasets? Any plans to move to higher-dim vectors in the next 6 months?
2) Re-ranking & reranking flow: do you do reranking client-side or in a separate microservice? Any latency budget for that hop?
3) Peak prompt length: you mentioned 600 tokens — can you share 95th percentile and max?
4) Are you currently doing any local caching of model outputs or prefix caching? If so, where?

I attached a short SOW draft and a quick pilot footprint recommendation — 2x A100-equivalent for initial throughput testing, with a streaming-enabled endpoint and embedding replica for reindex testing.

I can take point on the technical deep-dive; propose Wed Jun 17 10:00 PDT (we'll send an invite if that works).

— Aditya
